title: An agent records what a pane draws as a GIF
body:
decade's `screenshot` MCP tool captures one frame of what a pane draws, as a PNG at the screen's pixels, in `decade/src/server/compositor/screenshot.rs`. It asks the user first unless the pane accepts screenshots. A README for a terminal program needs motion too: a picker moving through a list, a bar filling up, a pointer selecting text. GitHub and crates.io both play a GIF embedded in a README. As far as we know, neither plays an `.mp4` linked from the repository.

## Proposal

- An MCP tool `record` starts capturing a pane's frames. A second call, or a duration given to the first, stops it and returns the path of the GIF.
- Each frame comes from the same offscreen render `screenshot` uses, taken whenever the pane's window commits a new frame. decade keeps each frame's time, so the GIF plays at the pace the program drew.
- decade draws the pointer into the frames while it is over the pane. Without it, a demo of a mouse feature shows text changing for no visible reason.
- `record` asks the user the way `screenshot` does, under an accept mode of its own.

## Rejected

- `vhs` drives a terminal in headless Chrome from a script. Its script has no mouse commands, so it cannot show selecting or clicking.
- `asciinema` with `agg` records a terminal's output and draws it again with `agg`'s own glyph renderer, not the terminal's. It shows no pointer.
- `gpu-screen-recorder` on a region of the screen works today. Someone has to find the pane's region by hand, and the region moves with the layout.

## Open

- decade could write the GIF itself with a crate such as `gif`, or hand the frames to `ffmpeg` with a generated palette. `ffmpeg`'s palette makes smaller, cleaner GIFs. A crate keeps decade from depending on an outside program.
- During a recording the person could drive the pane, or the agent could send scripted input, as the dev command from decade-56ee41 does for a server.
